steps.title: Photograph the bike before you start
steps.instruction: Walk around the bike and take close photos of the wiring, hoses, cable ties and clamps on both sides of the engine, plus the throttle cable and fuel line routing. These photos are your refit map, so take more than you think you need. Lay out labelled bags for each area: exhaust, tank and seat, subframe, wiring, drive side, clutch side, mounts.
verification: Photos clearly show every harness clip, tie and hose run on both sides.

steps.title: Lift the bike and strap it down
steps.instruction: Put the bike on the lift stand under the frame, below the engine, so that neither wheel touches the floor. Strap the frame to the stand or to an overhead point, because the bike loses its rear support when the swingarm pivot comes out later.
verification: Both wheels clear of the floor.
The bike does not rock when pushed at the bars and seat.

steps.title: Drain the oil from the bottom of the cases
steps.instruction: Set a pan under the engine. Remove the magnetic drain plug with its seal ring, the M16 screw plug with its O-ring, and the M20 plug that carries the long oil screen; leave any smaller screw beside the plugs alone. Let the oil run out completely while you look at the magnet and screen for debris.
verification: Magnet and screen inspected and photographed; debris noted.

steps.title: Pull the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the screws on the oil filter cover and lift the cover off with its O-ring. Pull the filter out of its housing with the lock ring pliers and let the housing drain. Bag the cover, screws and plugs together.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: With the engine cold and the bike upright, put a pan under the water pump cover. Take out the drain screw on the water pump cover, then remove the radiator cap so the system drains fully. Thread the drain screw back in by hand so it is not lost; it gets a new seal ring and its final torque when the engine is closed up.
verification: Drain screw back in finger-tight; radiator cap stored.

steps.title: Take off the seat
steps.instruction: Remove the seat fixing screw at the back. Lift the rear of the seat, slide it toward the tank to free the front, and lift it away.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel pump electrical connector. Blow dirt away from the fuel line quick coupling with compressed air, then release the coupling and fit the wash caps to both halves. A little fuel will run out, so have a rag ready and keep sparks away.

steps.title: Lift off the fuel tank
steps.instruction: Pull the breather hose off the tank lid. Remove the front tank screw with its rubber bushing and the two spoiler screws with their collar bushings. Ease both spoilers sideways off the radiators and lift the tank off without snagging the throttle cables.
verification: Tank off and stored away from the work area.

steps.title: Remove the air filter box cover
steps.instruction: If the cover is secured with a screw, remove it. Unclip the cover at its front edge, swing it sideways and forward, and take it off. Cover the air filter so nothing falls in.

steps.title: Take off the silencer
steps.instruction: Unhook the spring between the silencer and the header with the spring hook. Remove the silencer mounting screws with their washers and slide the silencer back off the header.
verification: Silencer off; screws, washers and spring bagged.

steps.title: Take off the header pipe
steps.instruction: Unhook the header springs at the cylinder head with the spring hook. Remove the screw that holds the header to the cylinder head brace and pull the header out of the exhaust port. Stuff a clean rag into the exhaust port.
verification: Header off; exhaust port plugged with a rag.

steps.title: Remove the frame protectors
steps.instruction: Cut the cable ties holding the frame protectors. Remove the screws with their washers, lift the left protector off, then push the right one forward and pull it out downward.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery negative
steps.instruction: Disconnect the negative cable from the 12-V battery and tuck it so it cannot spring back onto the terminal. Do this before any starter or harness connector is touched.

steps.title: Swing the subframe up
steps.instruction: Loosen the clamp on the intake boot where it meets the throttle body. On each side, loosen the lower subframe screw and remove the upper one. Pivot the subframe and airbox up and prop or tie it there, watching that the intake boot slides off the throttle body cleanly.
verification: Intake boot free of the throttle body and undamaged.

steps.title: Remove the engine braces
steps.instruction: Remove the screws holding the two engine braces (head stays) between the cylinder head and the frame and take the braces off. Keep the frame-side and engine-side screws apart, because they are different lengths and use different thread lockers at refit.
verification: Both braces off; screws bagged by position.

steps.title: Unplug the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Unplug the crankshaft speed sensor, alternator and gear position sensor connectors, cutting cable ties and opening clips as needed. Photograph each plug before you separate it. Free the harness so it can be pulled clear of the engine.
verification: All three engine harness connectors apart.
Harness free of the engine and photographed.

steps.title: Disconnect the starter cable
steps.instruction: Push back the protective cap on the starter motor terminal, remove the nut and lift off the positive cable. Hang the cable out of the way and thread the nut back onto the terminal so it is not lost.
verification: Starter cable off and clear of the engine.

steps.title: Unplug the cylinder head connectors
steps.instruction: Slide back the rubber cap on the sensor plug at the cylinder head and unplug it. Pull the spark plug connector off the plug. Move both leads clear of the head.
verification: Head sensor and spark plug connector disconnected.

steps.title: Pull the radiator hoses off the engine
steps.instruction: Loosen the two hose clamps where the radiator hoses join the engine and twist the hoses off. Some coolant will still run out, so keep a pan under the bike. Check the hose ends for cracks while they are off.
verification: Both hoses off the engine; hose ends inspected.

steps.title: Remove the engine sprocket cover
steps.instruction: Remove the two screws holding the engine sprocket cover and take the cover off. Note which screw is the M6 and which is the M8.

steps.title: Break the sprocket screw loose
steps.instruction: Have a helper press the rear brake pedal hard to lock the drive while you break the engine sprocket screw loose. Only loosen it at this point; the chain is what holds the sprocket still.
verification: Sprocket screw loose but still in.

steps.title: Split and remove the chain
steps.instruction: Find the master link, remove its clip and side plate, push the link out and lift the chain off both sprockets. Lay a rag over the swingarm and frame so the chain does not scratch them.
verification: Chain off; master link parts bagged.

steps.title: Take off the engine sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the loosened sprocket screw with its washer and slide the sprocket off the countershaft.
verification: Sprocket, screw and washer bagged together.

steps.title: Take off the shift lever
steps.instruction: Mark the lever and shaft with a paint pen so you can refit it on the same spline. Remove the pinch screw and washers and slide the lever off.
verification: Lever off and spline position marked.

steps.title: Unbolt the clutch slave cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the slave cylinder screws and lift it off the engine with its gasket, keeping the hydraulic line connected. Hang it on the frame without kinking the line, and zip-tie a spacer in the clutch lever so it cannot be pulled while the slave is off.
verification: Slave cylinder hanging free; line not kinked.

steps.title: Pull the throttle body off the head
steps.instruction: Loosen the clamp holding the throttle body to the cylinder head intake. Pull the throttle body straight back off the head and hang it on the frame with its cables and wiring still attached. Tape over the intake port and the throttle body opening.
verification: Throttle body free of the head and supported.

steps.title: Disconnect the linkage
steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm slightly with a block or helper to take the load off the linkage. Remove the nut and bolt joining the linkage lever to the angle lever.
verification: Linkage lever free of the angle lever; hardware bagged.

steps.title: Pull the swingarm pivot
steps.instruction: Check the chassis is still strapped down. Remove the swingarm pivot nut and drive or pull the pivot shaft out. Slide the swingarm back far enough to clear the engine and support it there, keeping the rear brake line free of kinks.
verification: Pivot shaft out; swingarm supported clear of the engine.
Chassis still stable on the stand.

steps.title: Check nothing is still attached
steps.instruction: Go around the engine with your photos and confirm no hose, wire, cable or tie still connects it to the frame. Wrap the frame tubes beside the engine with tape or rags to protect the finish.
verification: Nothing connects engine to chassis except the engine carrying screws.

steps.title: Lift the engine out
steps.instruction: With a helper holding the engine, remove the engine carrying screws. Tilt and lift the engine out of the frame to one side and set it on a clean, padded surface.
verification: Engine out without hitting the frame or radiators.
Chassis still stable on its stand.

steps.title: Mount the engine on the work stand
steps.instruction: Fit the holder and fitting to the engine work stand, then bolt the engine to it with the help of your helper or a hoist. Make sure it is tight before you put any wrench force on the engine.
verification: Engine solidly bolted to the work stand.
All chassis parts bagged and labelled.

prerequisites: Engine at room temperature, about 20 C (68 F), so the first valve clearance reading is valid.
Outside of the engine cleaned so no grit falls into the head or crankcase when it is opened.
A record sheet for clearances, shim sizes and every measurement in this guide.

Know which service you are doing: the minor service includes a new piston and a check of cylinder, head, camshaft, valve train and timing parts; the major service also renews the valves, springs, spring seats, retainers and timing chain.
critical_stop_conditions: Camshaft LOCK mark and crank notch do not line up together: you are on the wrong stroke or the chain has jumped; do not fit the locking screw by force.
Cylinder or head sealing face out of flat by more than 0.10 mm (0.0039 in): that part must be replaced.
Piston-to-cylinder clearance above the 0.120 mm (0.00472 in) wear limit, or a scored bore: do not reassemble with those parts.
Any rocker arm roller with radial play: replace that rocker before setting clearance.
Limit plug gauge slides easily into a valve guide, cracked seat or spark plug thread damage: hand the head to a machine shop.
Piston rings catch while sliding the piston in: stop and re-compress; never force it.
After assembly the engine does not turn over smoothly by hand through two full turns: stop and find the contact before going further.

steps.title: Clean around the head
steps.instruction: Blow and wipe all dirt from the valve cover, spark plug well and the joints between head, cylinder and cases. Grit that gets inside now ends up in the bearings later.

steps.title: Take out the spark plug
steps.instruction: Unscrew the spark plug with the spark plug wrench and link. Look at the plug firing end and note its colour and any oil or coolant residue.

steps.title: Open the crank access plug
steps.instruction: Unscrew the large screw plug in the alternator cover. This gives you access to turn the crankshaft.
verification: Access plug out; its seal set aside.

steps.title: Lift off the valve cover
steps.instruction: Remove the valve cover screws and lift the cover off together with its seal. Keep the seal on the cover if you plan to reuse it.

steps.title: Turn the engine to TDC
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise through the access hole until the LOCK mark on the camshaft gear lines up with the centre of the camshaft retaining bracket. Both rockers should be loose at this point, which tells you the piston is at top dead centre on compression.
verification: LOCK mark centred on the bracket.
Both rocker arms have free play.

steps.title: Lock the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Remove the crankshaft fixing screw plug and its sealing washer from the engine case. Look through the hole: the notch in the crank web must be visible. Screw in the crankshaft locking screw and snug it to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Locking screw installed and the crank cannot turn.

steps.title: Measure the valve clearance as found
steps.instruction: With the engine cold, slide feeler blades between each valve and its rocker arm and find the thickest blade that passes with a light drag. The spec is 0.10 to 0.15 mm (0.0039 to 0.0059 in) intake and 0.12 to 0.17 mm (0.0047 to 0.0067 in) exhaust. Write down all four readings with their positions; you need them to choose shims later.
verification: All four clearances recorded with position.

steps.title: Check the rocker rollers for play
steps.instruction: Hold each rocker arm and try to rock its roller up and down across its axle. No radial play is allowed; a roller that moves means that rocker arm gets replaced before any clearance work.
verification: Both rollers checked; any play recorded.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Unscrew the tensioner plug and take out its washer and spring to release the chain tension. Then remove the two mounting screws and lift the tensioner body off with its gasket.
verification: Tensioner, spring and plug out and bagged together.

steps.title: Remove the camshaft retaining bracket
steps.instruction: Remove the bracket screws and lift off the camshaft retaining bracket with its lock washer.

steps.title: Lift out the camshaft
steps.instruction: Press both rocker arms down slightly, ease the camshaft out of its bearing seat and slip the timing chain off the cam gear. Tie the chain up with a piece of wire so it cannot drop into the case.
verification: Chain tied up and not slack in the case.

steps.title: Unbolt the cylinder head
steps.instruction: Remove the single small M6 head screw first. Then loosen the M10 head screws a little at a time in a criss-cross order before taking them out with their washers.
verification: All head screws and washers out and bagged.

steps.title: Lift the head off
steps.instruction: Lift the head straight up, feeding the timing chain through its tunnel and keeping the chain wire held. Remove the dowels and the head gasket.
verification: Head off and on a clean surface.

steps.title: Raise the cylinder just enough
steps.instruction: Stuff a clean rag around the connecting rod in the case mouth. Slide the cylinder up only until the piston pin is exposed below the cylinder base.

steps.title: Push out the piston pin
steps.instruction: Remove one piston pin ring lock, push the pin out and lift the cylinder off with the piston still inside it. Push the piston out of the bore from the bottom, then peel off the base gasket.
verification: Case opening covered with a clean rag.

steps.title: Remove the rocker arms
steps.instruction: Remove the rocker shaft retaining screws. Thread an M6 screw into the end of each rocker shaft, pull the shaft out, and lift the rocker away. Tag each rocker and shaft intake or exhaust.
verification: Both rockers and shafts out and labelled.

steps.title: Lift out the shims
steps.instruction: Pick each shim off the top of its valve spring retainer and put it in a labelled tray slot for that exact valve. Read the thickness stamped on each and add it to your record.
verification: Four shims stored by position with thickness noted.

steps.title: Take the valves out
steps.instruction: Compress each valve spring with the valve spring compressor and insert, lift out the two collets and release the spring. Remove the retainer and spring, push the valve out through the combustion chamber, then pull off the stem seal and the spring seat. Keep every part of each valve together and labelled by position.
verification: All four valve sets out and stored by position.

steps.title: Clean the head and blow the oil passages
steps.instruction: Soak and brush off carbon from the chamber and ports without touching the valve seat faces with a scraper. Wash the head and blow compressed air through every oil passage to confirm they are clear.

steps.title: Check the head gasket face for warp
steps.instruction: Lay a straightedge across the head gasket face in several directions and try feeler blades under it. The limit is 0.10 mm (0.0039 in). Also look for cracks around the valve seats and spark plug thread.

steps.title: Check the valve guides
steps.instruction: Try the limit plug gauge in each valve guide. If the gauge slides in easily, that guide and its valve need replacing by a machine shop.
verification: All four guides checked and result recorded.

steps.title: Measure valve run-out and inspect the faces
steps.instruction: Spin each valve in V-blocks with a dial gauge on the edge of the valve head; run-out must not exceed 0.05 mm (0.002 in). Inspect the sealing face and the chrome stem, where wear usually shows up at the guide area.
verification: Run-out recorded for all four valves.

steps.title: Check the valve seat width
steps.instruction: Mark the valve face with a little marking compound, tap the valve against its seat and measure the contact band. Intake and exhaust are both specified at 2.00 mm (0.0787 in). A wide, narrow or broken band means the seat needs machining.
verification: Seat width recorded for each valve.

steps.title: Measure the valve springs and spring seats
steps.instruction: Look over each spring and spring seat for cracks or wear. Measure spring free length without the seat: at least 40.7 mm (1.602 in) for intake and exhaust. Measure spring seat thickness: 1.4 to 1.6 mm (0.055 to 0.063 in).
verification: Spring lengths and seat thicknesses recorded.
Out-of-spec parts set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Inspect the rocker shafts
steps.instruction: Check both rocker shafts and their bores for scoring, flats or other wear. Replace any shaft that is marked.

steps.title: Inspect the camshaft
steps.instruction: Examine the lobes and journals for pitting, scuffing or wear. If the surface is damaged, also check that oil reaches the camshaft and rockers before reassembly, because a blocked oiling path will ruin the new part.

steps.title: Hand off the cam bearings if rough
steps.instruction: Turn the camshaft bearings in the head by finger. If one feels rough or loose, take the bare head to a shop with the KTM camshaft-bearing press tools and ask for both bearings and the seal behind them to be renewed, with the small bearing pressed to its 1.4 mm (0.055 in) depth. Continue when it comes back.
verification: Bearings smooth, or head back from the shop with new bearings.

steps.title: Inspect the timing chain and rails
steps.instruction: With everything clean, check the cam gear and the crank timing sprocket teeth, the tensioning rail, guide rail and chain clip for grooves or breakage. Hang the chain and look for links that stay kinked. Replace anything worn; the chain is a replace item at the major service.

steps.title: Measure the cylinder bore
steps.instruction: Inspect the bore for scoring. Measure the bore at several heights in two directions at right angles to find any ovality, and read the size group stamped on the side of the cylinder. Size I is 95.000 to 95.012 mm (3.74015 to 3.74062 in); size II is 95.013 to 95.025 mm (3.74066 to 3.74113 in).
verification: All bore readings and the size group recorded.

steps.title: Check the cylinder head face for warp
steps.instruction: Lay the straightedge across the cylinder top face in several directions and try feeler blades underneath. The limit is 0.10 mm (0.0039 in).

steps.title: Measure the piston
steps.instruction: Mic the skirt 90 degrees across from the pin axis, 7 mm (0.28 in) up from its lower edge. Size I is 94.93 to 94.96 mm (3.7374 to 3.7386 in) and size II is 94.94 to 94.97 mm (3.7378 to 3.739 in); the group is marked beside the pin boss. Do this for the old piston and for a new one if you have it.

steps.title: Work out piston-to-cylinder clearance
steps.instruction: Subtract the largest piston reading from the smallest bore reading for the tightest clearance, and the smallest piston reading from the largest bore reading for the loosest. New fit is 0.040 to 0.082 mm (size I) or 0.043 to 0.085 mm (size II); the wear limit is 0.120 mm (0.00472 in).
verification: Both clearance figures recorded and compared with spec.

steps.title: Check ring groove clearance and end gap
steps.instruction: With the rings on the piston, measure the gap between each ring and its groove; the limit is 0.08 mm (0.0031 in). Then push each ring squarely into the bore with the piston to 10 mm (0.39 in) below the top and read the gap between the ring ends: no more than 1.00 mm (0.0394 in) for the top ring and 1.20 mm (0.0472 in) for the oil ring. If the gap is over but the bore is in spec, replace the rings.
verification: Groove clearances and end gaps recorded.

steps.title: Check the piston pin fit
steps.instruction: Look for blueing or wear on the pin. Slide it into the connecting rod small end and then into the piston and feel for rocking play. Play in the rod means rod and pin work; play in the piston means a new piston and pin.
verification: Pin fit recorded for rod and piston.

steps.title: Fit the valves back into the head
steps.instruction: Fit each spring seat, then press a new stem seal onto each guide. Oil each valve stem and slide it into its original guide, fit the spring and retainer, compress the spring and set the collets with a dab of grease. Release slowly and tap the stem end lightly with a soft mallet to confirm the collets are locked.
verification: All four valves fitted in their original positions.

steps.title: Put the shims back
steps.instruction: Place each shim back on its own valve spring retainer. Use the original shims for now; you will correct them after the clearance check.
verification: Shims back in their original positions.

steps.title: Fit the rocker arms
steps.instruction: Set each rocker in place and push its shaft in with the threaded hole facing out. The shaft with the oil hole goes on the intake side and the cut-outs face up. Line up the holes in the shafts with the screw holes in the head, take out the M6 puller screw and torque the rocker shaft screws to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).

steps.title: Decide whether to open the bottom end
steps.instruction: Look at your records and the service hours. If you found metal in the oil, the crank or gearbox needs attention, or this is the major service, pause here and run the "Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps" job now, then come back to the next step. Otherwise carry on.
verification: Decision recorded: top end only, or bottom end first.

steps.title: Prepare for the cylinder
steps.instruction: Confirm the crank is locked at TDC with the locking screw and the timing chain is tied up. Clean the case gasket face and check the dowels are in place. Lay a new base gasket over the dowels.
verification: Crank locked; base gasket on the dowels.

steps.title: Load the piston into the cylinder
steps.instruction: Fit the rings with their markings facing up and turn the ring gaps 180 degrees apart. Fit one new ring lock in the piston. Oil the piston and bore, squeeze the rings fully with the ring compressor, and push the piston crown-first into the bottom of the upturned cylinder until the pin bore just sits below the cylinder base.
verification: Piston in the bore with rings undamaged.
Pin bore still exposed below the cylinder.

steps.title: Join the piston to the rod
steps.instruction: Lower the cylinder over the rod with the piston marking toward the exhaust side, feeding the timing chain up through its tunnel. Oil the pin, push it through piston and rod, and set the second new ring lock with the insertion tool, pressing it into the groove and turning it home. Check the ring lock is fully in its groove at both ends.

steps.title: Slide the cylinder down
steps.instruction: Pull the rag from the case. Keep the timing chain taut and slide the cylinder down over the dowels onto the new base gasket.
verification: Cylinder seated flat on the gasket.
Chain still taut and tied up.

steps.title: Set the head in place
steps.instruction: Fit the head dowels and a new head gasket. Lower the head over the dowels, feeding the chain through, and keep the chain wire held.
verification: Head sitting flat on the gasket.

steps.title: Torque the head screws
steps.instruction: Oil the threads and collars of the M10 head screws and fit them with their washers; start the small M6 screw but leave it loose. Tighten the M10 screws in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), then 30 Nm (22.1 lb-ft), then 50 Nm (36.9 lb-ft). Finally torque the M6 screw to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: All three stages done on every M10 screw; sign off on the record sheet.

steps.title: Fit the camshaft in time
steps.instruction: With the crank still locked, pull the chain up, fit the camshaft and wrap the chain over the cam gear. The LOCK mark on the cam must face up and sit flush with the mark in the head with no slack on the front run of the chain. Fit the lock washer and bracket and torque the bracket screws to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).
verification: LOCK mark flush with the head mark.

steps.title: Fit the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Fit the tensioner body with a new gasket and torque its two screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Insert the spring and refit the plug with its seal ring, torqued to 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Turn the engine and re-check timing
steps.instruction: Take out the crank locking screw. Turn the crank counterclockwise through several full turns by hand, feeling for any hard spot, and bring it back to TDC. Confirm the cam LOCK mark lines up with the centre of the bracket at the same moment the crank notch shows in the hole, then fit the locking screw again at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Cam and crank marks line up together.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance
steps.instruction: Measure all four clearances again with the feeler gauge and write them down. Intake must be 0.10 to 0.15 mm and exhaust 0.12 to 0.17 mm, engine cold.

steps.title: Work out any new shims
steps.instruction: For a valve out of range, take its shim thickness, add the measured clearance and subtract the clearance you are aiming for, ideally the middle of the range. That gives the shim size to fit. Write the new size beside the old one.
verification: New shim size listed for every out-of-range valve.

steps.title: Swap the shims
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner and camshaft again with the crank locked, as before. Lift each rocker at its outer end, swap the shim for the calculated size, and refit the camshaft in time and the tensioner with another new gasket at the same torques.

steps.title: Confirm the final clearances
steps.instruction: Turn the engine over several times, return it to TDC and measure all four valves once more. Repeat the shim swap until every valve is in range, and record the final readings.
verification: All four clearances in range and recorded.

steps.title: Remove the crank lock
steps.instruction: Take out the crankshaft locking screw and fit the screw plug with its sealing washer, torqued to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the valve cover
steps.instruction: Fit the engine vent gasket into the valve cover and set the cover in place with its seal. Torque the valve cover screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the spark plug and access plug
steps.instruction: Fit the spark plug with the plug wrench at 10 to 12 Nm (7.4 to 8.9 lb-ft). Refit the screw plug in the alternator cover at 18 Nm (13.3 lb-ft).
verification: Spark plug and alternator cover plug torqued.

steps.title: Install the oil filter
steps.instruction: Tilt the engine on its stand and fill the oil filter housing about one third with engine oil. Push in the new filter, oil the cover O-ring, fit the cover and torque its screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the oil screens and plugs
steps.instruction: Slide the long oil screen with its O-rings onto a pin wrench, guide it through the plug hole until it is fully home in the far case half, and fit the M20 plug with its O-ring at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft). Fit the M16 plug with a new O-ring at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft) and the magnetic drain plug with a new seal ring at 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft).
verification: All three plugs torqued with new seals.

steps.title: Seal the coolant drain screw
steps.instruction: Fit a new seal ring to the coolant drain screw on the water pump cover, apply Loctite 243 and torque it to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Drain screw at 10 Nm with new seal ring.

steps.title: Final bench check
steps.instruction: Turn the engine slowly through two full turns by the rotor screw to feel for anything binding. Check every opening is closed or capped, and bag the record sheet with the engine.

entry_state: Engine out of the frame, drained, on an engine work stand (exit of the "Take the engine out of the frame" job).

completeness: Covers locking the engine at TDC, removing and refitting the tensioner, camshaft, rockers, head, valves, cylinder and piston, every printed top-end measurement, and the valve clearance check and shim swap; cam bearing replacement, valve guide replacement and seat machining are hand-offs.

Camshaft bearing pressing in the head (hand-off step)
Cylinder replating or boring
Bottom-end work (separate guide)
Throttle body and injector service

prerequisites: Engine at room temperature, about 20 C (68 F), so the first valve clearance reading is valid.
Outside of the engine cleaned so no grit falls into the head or crankcase when it is opened.
A record sheet for clearances, shim sizes and every measurement in this guide.

Know which service you are doing: the minor service includes a new piston and a check of cylinder, head, camshaft, valve train and timing parts; the major service also renews the valves, springs, spring seats, retainers and timing chain.
critical_stop_conditions: Camshaft LOCK mark and crank notch do not line up together: you are on the wrong stroke or the chain has jumped; do not fit the locking screw by force.
Cylinder or head sealing face out of flat by more than 0.10 mm (0.0039 in): that part must be replaced.
Piston-to-cylinder clearance above the 0.120 mm (0.00472 in) wear limit, or a scored bore: do not reassemble with those parts.
Any rocker arm roller with radial play: replace that rocker before setting clearance.
Limit plug gauge slides easily into a valve guide, cracked seat or spark plug thread damage: hand the head to a machine shop.
Piston rings catch while sliding the piston in: stop and re-compress; never force it.
After assembly the engine does not turn over smoothly by hand through two full turns: stop and find the contact before going further.

steps.title: Check ring groove clearance and end gap
steps.instruction: With the rings on the piston, measure the gap between each ring and its groove; the limit is 0.08 mm (0.0031 in). Then push each ring squarely into the bore with the piston to 10 mm (0.39 in) below the top and read the gap between the ring ends: no more than 1.00 mm (0.0394 in) for the top ring and 1.20 mm (0.0472 in) for the oil ring. If the gap is over but the bore is in spec, replace the rings.
verification: Groove clearances and end gaps recorded.

steps.title: Check the piston pin fit
steps.instruction: Look for blueing or wear on the pin. Slide it into the connecting rod small end and then into the piston and feel for rocking play. Play in the rod means rod and pin work; play in the piston means a new piston and pin.
verification: Pin fit recorded for rod and piston.

steps.title: Fit the valves back into the head
steps.instruction: Fit each spring seat, then press a new stem seal onto each guide. Oil each valve stem and slide it into its original guide, fit the spring and retainer, compress the spring and set the collets with a dab of grease. Release slowly and tap the stem end lightly with a soft mallet to confirm the collets are locked.
verification: All four valves fitted in their original positions.

steps.title: Put the shims back
steps.instruction: Place each shim back on its own valve spring retainer. Use the original shims for now; you will correct them after the clearance check.
verification: Shims back in their original positions.

steps.title: Fit the rocker arms
steps.instruction: Set each rocker in place and push its shaft in with the threaded hole facing out. The shaft with the oil hole goes on the intake side and the cut-outs face up. Line up the holes in the shafts with the screw holes in the head, take out the M6 puller screw and torque the rocker shaft screws to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).

steps.title: Decide whether to open the bottom end
steps.instruction: Look at your records and the service hours. If you found metal in the oil, the crank or gearbox needs attention, or this is the major service, pause here and run the "Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps" job now, then come back to the next step. Otherwise carry on.
verification: Decision recorded: top end only, or bottom end first.

steps.title: Prepare for the cylinder
steps.instruction: Confirm the crank is locked at TDC with the locking screw and the timing chain is tied up. Clean the case gasket face and check the dowels are in place. Lay a new base gasket over the dowels.
verification: Crank locked; base gasket on the dowels.

steps.title: Load the piston into the cylinder
steps.instruction: Fit the rings with their markings facing up and turn the ring gaps 180 degrees apart. Fit one new ring lock in the piston. Oil the piston and bore, squeeze the rings fully with the ring compressor, and push the piston crown-first into the bottom of the upturned cylinder until the pin bore just sits below the cylinder base.
verification: Piston in the bore with rings undamaged.
Pin bore still exposed below the cylinder.

steps.title: Join the piston to the rod
steps.instruction: Lower the cylinder over the rod with the piston marking toward the exhaust side, feeding the timing chain up through its tunnel. Oil the pin, push it through piston and rod, and set the second new ring lock with the insertion tool, pressing it into the groove and turning it home. Check the ring lock is fully in its groove at both ends.

steps.title: Slide the cylinder down
steps.instruction: Pull the rag from the case. Keep the timing chain taut and slide the cylinder down over the dowels onto the new base gasket.
verification: Cylinder seated flat on the gasket.
Chain still taut and tied up.

steps.title: Set the head in place
steps.instruction: Fit the head dowels and a new head gasket. Lower the head over the dowels, feeding the chain through, and keep the chain wire held.
verification: Head sitting flat on the gasket.

steps.title: Torque the head screws
steps.instruction: Oil the threads and collars of the M10 head screws and fit them with their washers; start the small M6 screw but leave it loose. Tighten the M10 screws in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), then 30 Nm (22.1 lb-ft), then 50 Nm (36.9 lb-ft). Finally torque the M6 screw to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: All three stages done on every M10 screw; sign off on the record sheet.

steps.title: Fit the camshaft in time
steps.instruction: With the crank still locked, pull the chain up, fit the camshaft and wrap the chain over the cam gear. The LOCK mark on the cam must face up and sit flush with the mark in the head with no slack on the front run of the chain. Fit the lock washer and bracket and torque the bracket screws to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).
verification: LOCK mark flush with the head mark.

steps.title: Fit the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Fit the tensioner body with a new gasket and torque its two screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Insert the spring and refit the plug with its seal ring, torqued to 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Turn the engine and re-check timing
steps.instruction: Take out the crank locking screw. Turn the crank counterclockwise through several full turns by hand, feeling for any hard spot, and bring it back to TDC. Confirm the cam LOCK mark lines up with the centre of the bracket at the same moment the crank notch shows in the hole, then fit the locking screw again at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Cam and crank marks line up together.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance
steps.instruction: Measure all four clearances again with the feeler gauge and write them down. Intake must be 0.10 to 0.15 mm and exhaust 0.12 to 0.17 mm, engine cold.

steps.title: Work out any new shims
steps.instruction: For a valve out of range, take its shim thickness, add the measured clearance and subtract the clearance you are aiming for, ideally the middle of the range. That gives the shim size to fit. Write the new size beside the old one.
verification: New shim size listed for every out-of-range valve.

steps.title: Swap the shims
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner and camshaft again with the crank locked, as before. Lift each rocker at its outer end, swap the shim for the calculated size, and refit the camshaft in time and the tensioner with another new gasket at the same torques.

steps.title: Confirm the final clearances
steps.instruction: Turn the engine over several times, return it to TDC and measure all four valves once more. Repeat the shim swap until every valve is in range, and record the final readings.
verification: All four clearances in range and recorded.

steps.title: Remove the crank lock
steps.instruction: Take out the crankshaft locking screw and fit the screw plug with its sealing washer, torqued to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the valve cover
steps.instruction: Fit the engine vent gasket into the valve cover and set the cover in place with its seal. Torque the valve cover screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the spark plug and access plug
steps.instruction: Fit the spark plug with the plug wrench at 10 to 12 Nm (7.4 to 8.9 lb-ft). Refit the screw plug in the alternator cover at 18 Nm (13.3 lb-ft).
verification: Spark plug and alternator cover plug torqued.

steps.title: Install the oil filter
steps.instruction: Tilt the engine on its stand and fill the oil filter housing about one third with engine oil. Push in the new filter, oil the cover O-ring, fit the cover and torque its screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the oil screens and plugs
steps.instruction: Slide the long oil screen with its O-rings onto a pin wrench, guide it through the plug hole until it is fully home in the far case half, and fit the M20 plug with its O-ring at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft). Fit the M16 plug with a new O-ring at 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft) and the magnetic drain plug with a new seal ring at 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft).
verification: All three plugs torqued with new seals.

steps.title: Seal the coolant drain screw
steps.instruction: Fit a new seal ring to the coolant drain screw on the water pump cover, apply Loctite 243 and torque it to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Drain screw at 10 Nm with new seal ring.

steps.title: Final bench check
steps.instruction: Turn the engine slowly through two full turns by the rotor screw to feel for anything binding. Check every opening is closed or capped, and bag the record sheet with the engine.

entry_state: Engine on the work stand with the cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed, oil drained, filter out and crank locked at TDC with the locking screw (the top-end guide the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job paused at step branch-bottom-end).
Engine sprocket, shift lever and clutch slave cylinder already off (done in the "Take the engine out of the frame" job).
exit_state: Bottom end rebuilt and closed on the work stand: cases sealed, crank end play recorded in spec, gears shift through all positions, oil pumps, timing chain, rails, primary drive, clutch, balancer, water pump, rotor, clutch and alternator covers, push rod and starter fitted. Crank locked at TDC and the timing chain tied up. Return to the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job at step prep-cylinder-fit.
title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps
completeness: Covers stripping both sides, splitting the cases, inspecting and measuring the crank, gearbox, shift parts, clutch, pumps and starter drive, changing case bearings and seals, and closing the cases; the connecting rod and crank pin pressing job is a specialist hand-off.
excluded: Pressing the crankshaft apart and rebuilding the connecting rod (specialist hand-off)
Crankcase repair or welding
Stator rewinding or electrical testing beyond the starter bench test
XC-F US six-speed gearbox (different gear stack)
Top-end work (separate guide)

Oven able to hold 150 C (302 F) for case halves, and a flat wooden board

Dial gauge with magnetic or case-mounted stand, V-blocks or roller blocks
Feeler gauge (KTM 79129941000 or equivalent) and straightedge
12-V power supply with leads for the starter test

required_parts.purpose: Gearbox lock rings are replaced every time.

required_parts.purpose: Replaced at the major service.

required_parts.purpose: Chain is renewed at the major service; the sprocket is usually ruined if pulled off the crank.

required_parts.name: Freewheel

required_parts.purpose: For the specialist crank rebuild at the major service.
