prerequisites: Top end removed per the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job up to step branch-bottom-end.
Spotless bench, plenty of labelled trays, and a phone to photograph each layer before it comes apart.
Access to an oven for heating the case halves and a press or a shop that has one.
Arrangements made with a crankshaft specialist if the crank needs rebuilding.
critical_stop_conditions: Any new case bearing that is loose in its bore once the case has cooled: that case half must be replaced, not glued.
Crank run-out above 0.03 mm (0.0012 in) at either bearing pin, or rod side play outside 0.20 to 0.45 mm: crank goes to the specialist.
Crank end play outside 0.50 to 0.80 mm after shimming: do not seal the cases.
Oil pump rotor clearances over 0.20 mm (0.0079 in), or oil pressure valve spring shorter than 22.1 mm (0.87 in): replace before assembly.
Case halves will not close without pulling them together with the screws: stop, split again and find the misplaced part.
Gearbox will not shift through every gear on the bench, or the balancer marks cannot be aligned with the crank at TDC: stop before fitting the clutch cover.
Never clamp the crank by its pin in a vise and hammer on it; the webs twist and the crank is scrap.

steps.title: Confirm the starting position
steps.instruction: Check the crank is locked at TDC with the locking screw, the case mouth is covered with a clean rag and the timing chain is tied up. Photograph the clutch side and the alternator side before anything comes off.

steps.title: Remove the starter motor
steps.instruction: Remove the starter motor screws and pull the motor out of the case. Bag it with its screws.

steps.title: Pull out the clutch push rod
steps.instruction: Slide the clutch push rod out of the main shaft from the slave cylinder side and keep it straight and clean.

steps.title: Remove the water pump cover
steps.instruction: Remove the screws from the water pump cover, noting which screw goes where by length, and lift the cover off with its gasket.

steps.title: Remove the impeller
steps.instruction: Undo the nut on the impeller and pull the impeller off its shaft.

steps.title: Take off the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover screws and draw the cover off; the balancer shaft comes out with it. Lift the gasket and keep the dowels.

steps.title: Unload the clutch spring retainer
steps.instruction: Back the spring retainer screws out a little at a time in a criss-cross order so the diaphragm spring unloads evenly. Lift off the spring retainer, the spring washer, the pretension ring and the pressure cap.
verification: All four parts off and kept in order.

steps.title: Take out the clutch discs
steps.instruction: Pull the whole friction and steel stack out in one go and lay it down in its stacking order. Remove the clutch throw-out.

steps.title: Undo the inner hub nut
steps.instruction: Lock the clutch center with the KTM holding wrench and crack the hub nut loose. Remove the nut and its wedge lock washers.

steps.title: Remove the hub and basket
steps.instruction: Slide off the inner hub and the thrust washer behind it, which often sticks to the hub. Pull the clutch basket off, then remove the needle bearing and collar bushing.
verification: Hub, washer, basket, needle bearing and bushing out and kept together.

steps.title: Remove the torque limiter and starter idler
steps.instruction: Undo the screw and washer that retain the torque limiter, then lift off the limiter together with the starter idler (intermediate) gear.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump idler gear
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and washer from the oil pump idler shaft and slide the idler gear off with its washer.

steps.title: Remove the gear locking lever
steps.instruction: Undo the locking lever screw and take it out together with the lever, washer, sleeve and spring.

steps.title: Remove the shift drum locating unit
steps.instruction: Remove its screw, push the shift shaft sliding plate away from the locating unit, and lift the unit off the end of the shift drum.

steps.title: Pull out the shift shaft
steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft assembly out of the case with its washer.

steps.title: Undo the primary gear nut
steps.instruction: The primary gear nut has a left-hand thread, so turn it clockwise to loosen. With the crank still locked, break it free and remove it.

steps.title: Pull the primary gear
steps.instruction: Put the protection cap in the crank end, fit the primary gear puller and draw the gear off. Lift out the woodruff key and the freewheel gear behind it.
verification: Primary gear, key and freewheel gear off.

steps.title: Remove the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Remove the alternator cover screws and lift the cover off with its gasket. The stator stays in the cover.

steps.title: Pull the rotor
steps.instruction: With the crank still locked, remove the rotor screw. Fit the protection cap into the crank end, thread the rotor puller into the rotor, hold the puller body and turn its centre screw in until the rotor pops free. Keep the woodruff key.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain and rails
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioning rail screw and rail, then the guide rail screw, guide rails and chain clip. If the chain will be reused, mark its running direction with paint, then lift it off the crank sprocket.
verification: Chain and rails out; direction marked if reusing.

steps.title: Remove the gear position sensor
steps.instruction: Remove the two screws and take the gear position sensor off together with its protective plate.

steps.title: Remove the main shaft circlip and bushing
steps.instruction: Take the lock ring off the end of the gearbox main shaft and slide off the bushing.

steps.title: Remove the suction pump
steps.instruction: Remove the pump cover screws, the cover and its O-ring. Mark the outer face of the rotors with a felt pen, then lift out the inner and outer rotor and the drive pin.
verification: Rotors out with orientation marked; pin kept.

steps.title: Remove the force pump
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and washer from the pump drive gear, slide the gear off and take out its pin. Remove the pump cover screws and cover, draw the pump shaft out until its second pin clears the inner rotor, take that pin out, then lift out the rotors and the shaft.
verification: Force pump parts out and kept together.

steps.title: Take out the crank locking screw
steps.instruction: Remove the crankshaft locking screw; the cases cannot separate while it is engaged.

steps.title: Remove the case screws
steps.instruction: Push the case screws through a cardboard template of the case outline as you remove them, so each length goes back in its own hole.
verification: All case screws out and mapped.

steps.title: Split the cases
steps.instruction: Tilt the engine so the left case half is up, and remove the work-stand fixing arm fitting from it. Bolt the case splitting puller to the left half with suitable screws and draw the half off evenly, tapping the shaft ends if needed. Never pry between the sealing faces, and keep the half from tilting as it comes off.
verification: Left case half off without damage.

steps.title: Remove the shift rails
steps.instruction: Pull both shift rails out with their springs.

steps.title: Remove the shift drum and forks
steps.instruction: Swing the forks aside, lift the shift drum out, then take out the forks. Keep each fork's roller on its pin and tag each fork with its position.
verification: Drum and forks out; rollers kept; positions tagged.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Lift the main shaft and countershaft out together with their O-ring and washer. Check the bearing for the washer if it is not on the shaft.
verification: Both shafts out as a pair; washer found.

steps.title: Lift out the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift the crankshaft out of the right case half, then take the right half off the work stand.

steps.title: Clean the case halves
steps.instruction: Remove every trace of old sealant from both joint faces with a plastic scraper and solvent, without gouging the aluminium. Wash both halves.

steps.title: Check the oil pressure control valve
steps.instruction: Unscrew the oil pressure control valve plug from the right case and take out the spring and ball. The spring must be at least 22.1 mm (0.87 in) long. Refit the ball and spring and torque the plug with a new sealing washer to 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft) after the case work is finished.
verification: Valve refitted at 20 Nm with new washer.

steps.title: Strip the right case half
steps.instruction: Remove the remaining dowels, the piston-cooling oil nozzle, and the bearing retainer screws and retainers over the main shaft, countershaft and shift drum bearings.
verification: Retainers and nozzle out; bearings exposed.

steps.title: Heat out the right case bearings
steps.instruction: Heat the clean right case half evenly in an oven to 150 C (302 F). Wearing heat gloves, rap the case flat onto a wooden board so the bearings drop out, and pull any that stay with a bearing puller. Take out the washer behind the bearing.
verification: All bearings due for replacement out.

steps.title: Fit new bearings in the right case
steps.instruction: Reheat the case to 150 C (302 F), refit the washer, and drop the new bearings in cold. Lay the case flat and, if needed, press them home only on the outer race until they are fully seated or flush. Let the case cool and check every bearing is tight in its bore.
verification: All bearings seated and tight when cold.

steps.title: Refit the right case retainers and nozzle
steps.instruction: Refit the bearing retainers with Loctite 243 on the screws at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Refit the piston-cooling oil nozzle with Loctite 243 at 2 Nm (1.5 lb-ft), then blow air through every oil channel.

steps.title: Strip the left case half
steps.instruction: Remove the remaining dowels, the oil spray tube and its screw, the bearing retainers, and the countershaft and shift shaft seals.

steps.title: Change the left case bearings
steps.instruction: Heat the half to 150 C (302 F) and drop the bearings out on the wooden board as before. Reheat, refit the washer, set the new cold bearings in and press home on the outer race only with the case flat. Check they are tight once cool.

steps.title: Fit the left case seals and retainers
steps.instruction: Press the new countershaft and shift shaft seals in, open side inward, until flush. Refit the bearing retainers with Loctite 243 at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and the oil spray tube screw with Loctite 243 at 2 Nm (1.5 lb-ft). Refit the dowels and blow out every oil channel.

steps.title: Renew the crank seal in the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and the old crankshaft seal from the clutch cover. Press the new seal in, open side inward, until flush, refit the lock ring and grease the sealing lip.
verification: New seal flush; lock ring seated.

steps.title: Strip the water pump
steps.instruction: Remove the balancer shaft and the water pump shaft seal from the clutch cover. Support the cover properly and press the water pump shaft bearing out toward the inside.
verification: Seal and bearing out without cracking the cover.

steps.title: Rebuild the water pump
steps.instruction: With the cover supported, press the new bearing in to its stop with the bearing pressing tool. Press the new seal fully in with the seal tool so its narrower chamfer faces the balancer shaft.
verification: Seal fully home, correct way round.

steps.title: Fit the balancer shaft into the cover
steps.instruction: Inspect the balancer shaft gear and bearing surfaces. Fit the protection cap over the water pump shaft end, slide the balancer shaft into place without cutting the seals, and remove the cap.

steps.title: Measure the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Set the crank on roller blocks with a dial gauge on each main bearing pin and turn it slowly: run-out must not exceed 0.03 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the side play between the rod big end and the crank web with a feeler gauge: 0.20 to 0.45 mm (0.0079 to 0.0177 in). Check the big end for any up-and-down play and the timing sprocket teeth for wear.

steps.title: Send the crank to a specialist if needed
steps.instruction: If any reading is out, the big end has play, or this is the major service, take the crank to a crankshaft specialist. Ask for a new rod, bearing and crank pin with the pin oil hole lined up with the web oil hole, side play set to 0.20 to 0.45 mm, run-out trued to 0.03 mm or less at both bearing pins, and the main bearing inner races and timing sprocket renewed if you are changing the case bearings or chain. Ask for the thickness of the compensating disks behind each inner race to be written down, and continue when it comes back.
verification: Crank back with a written record, or crank passed inspection.

steps.title: Check crank end play
steps.instruction: Oil the main bearings, set the crank into the right case half with the dowels in, and fit the left half dry with no sealant. Torque the case screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Mount a dial gauge on the crank end and push and pull the crank: end play must be 0.50 to 0.80 mm (0.0197 to 0.0315 in).

steps.title: Correct end play if needed
steps.instruction: If the end play is too small, the alternator-side inner race comes off and a compensating disk is removed; if too large, one is added. The clutch side normally carries a 0.2 mm disk. Pull and refit the inner race with the heated puller (heat it to 150 C (302 F) for removal and 120 C (248 F) for fitting), or have the specialist do it, then re-check and split the cases again.
verification: End play in range and recorded.

steps.title: Measure both oil pumps
steps.instruction: Fit each pump's rotors in their bores and use feeler blades between the outer rotor and the case, and between the outer and inner rotor. Both gaps must be 0.20 mm (0.0079 in) or less. Replace the suction pump regardless at the major service.

steps.title: Strip the main shaft
steps.instruction: Clamp the main shaft in soft jaws with the geared end down. Remove the parts one at a time and lay them out in order on a clean rag, photographing as you go: stop disk, second gear, fourth gear, needle bearing, stop disk, lock ring, third gear, lock ring, stop disk, fifth gear and its bushing.

steps.title: Strip the countershaft
steps.instruction: Clamp the countershaft the same way and remove the parts in order: stop disk, first gear, needle bearing, stop disk, fifth gear, lock ring, stop disk, third gear, needle bearing, stop disk, lock ring, fourth gear, lock ring, stop disk, second gear and needle bearing. Lay them out in order.

steps.title: Inspect the gearbox
steps.instruction: Check every needle bearing, the shaft journals and splines, the gear teeth and the gear bores for pitting, chips or bluing. Look at the engagement dogs and slots: rounded or chipped dogs mean that gear pair is replaced. Slide each sliding gear on its shaft splines; it must move freely. Check the stop disks for wear.
verification: Each gear pair passed or tagged for replacement.

steps.title: Inspect the shift drum, forks and rails
steps.instruction: Look at the fork pads for wear or bluing and the drum grooves for wear. Check the drum turns smoothly in its bearing. Roll the fork rails on a flat surface for bend and check their springs, and slide each fork on its rail for scoring or stiffness.
verification: Forks, drum and rails passed or tagged.

steps.title: Check the shift shaft
steps.instruction: Grip the shift shaft by its short end in soft vise jaws. Fit the sliding plate guide-pin down onto the shift quadrant, then the pressure spring, spring guide, return spring with its offset end up and over the abutment bolt, and the stop disk. Check the sliding plate contact areas and return surface for notches, then measure the gap between the sliding plate and the quadrant: 0.40 to 0.80 mm (0.0157 to 0.0315 in).

steps.title: Check the starter drive
steps.instruction: Inspect the teeth and bearings of the starter intermediate gear, torque limiter and freewheel gear. Briefly connect the starter motor to a 12-V supply, case to negative and terminal to positive; it must spin. Fit a new O-ring to the starter.

steps.title: Check or change the freewheel
steps.instruction: Fit the freewheel gear into the back of the primary gear while turning the primary gear clockwise. The primary gear must turn clockwise and lock counterclockwise. To change the freewheel, squeeze off its expansion ring, take out the old one, oil and fit the new one facing the same way, and refit the ring so all its lugs pass through the freewheel slots into the groove.
verification: Freewheel locks in one direction only.

steps.title: Inspect the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Check the throw-out, the push rod on a flat surface for bend, the spring retainer, spring washer, pretension ring and pressure cap for wear. Check the inner hub, the damping rubbers and the basket slots for notching, and the needle bearing and bushing. Steels must be flat and unpitted and frictions free of bluing or scoring; measure the pack thickness, which must be at least 26.4 mm (1.039 in).

steps.title: Rebuild the main shaft
steps.instruction: Oil every part and use new lock rings. With the geared end down in soft jaws, fit the needle bearing and fifth gear, a stop disk and lock ring, third gear with its collar down, a lock ring, a stop disk and needle bearing, fourth gear, second gear and a final stop disk. Spin every gear to check it turns freely.
verification: Stack matches the order; all gears free.

steps.title: Rebuild the countershaft
steps.instruction: With the toothed end down in soft jaws, fit the needle bearing and second gear, stop disk and lock ring, fourth gear with its fork groove down, lock ring and stop disk, needle bearing and third gear, stop disk and lock ring, fifth gear and stop disk, needle bearing and first gear, and a final stop disk. Spin every gear to check it turns freely.
verification: Stack matches the order; all gears free.

steps.title: Set the crank into the right case
steps.instruction: Mount the right case half on the work stand. Oil the main bearing and lower the crankshaft into it.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Oil the gearbox bearings and drop both gearbox shafts in as a pair, making sure the washer and O-ring are on.

steps.title: Fit the forks, drum and rails
steps.instruction: Put the fork with the smaller bore into the main shaft groove, and the other two into the lower and upper countershaft grooves. Drop the shift drum into its bearing, swing each fork's roller into its drum track, and slide both rails in with their springs.
verification: Every roller in its drum track.

steps.title: Apply case sealant
steps.instruction: Check the dowels are in, degrease both joint faces and lay a thin, even bead of Loctite 5910 on the left case half.

steps.title: Close the cases
steps.instruction: Lower the left half over the shafts, tapping lightly with a rubber mallet while turning the gearbox shafts until the faces meet; never use the screws to draw the halves together. Fit the M6x80 screws, then the M6x65 screws, and torque them all in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Refit the cap on the work-stand fixing arm.

steps.title: Fit the suction pump
steps.instruction: Oil the pump shaft and rotors. Slide the pump shaft in, fit the needle roller, fit the suction pump rotors as marked, a new O-ring and the cover, and torque the cover screws with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the main shaft bushing and circlip
steps.instruction: Slide the bushing onto the main shaft and fit a new lock ring.
verification: Lock ring fully in its groove.

steps.title: Lock the crank at TDC again
steps.instruction: Turn the crank until the notch shows in the locking screw hole and screw the crankshaft locking screw in.

steps.title: Fit the force pump
steps.instruction: Oil the rotors and fit them with the rounded side toward the case, then fit the pin. Fit the cover with its part number facing out and torque the screws with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Fit the drive pin, the pump gear, its washer and the lock ring, and turn the gear by hand to check it is free.

steps.title: Fit the gear position sensor
steps.instruction: Fit the gear position sensor with its protective plate and torque the screws with Loctite 243 to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the timing chain and rails
steps.instruction: Loop the chain onto the crank sprocket, keeping the marked direction if reused. Fit the guide rails and chain clip and torque the clip screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the tensioning rail and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Tie the chain up.

steps.title: Fit the primary gear
steps.instruction: Fit the freewheel gear and the woodruff key, then slide the primary gear on with its slot over the key. Thread on the left-hand nut (turn counterclockwise) and torque it to 120 Nm (88.5 lb-ft) with the crank locked.
verification: Primary nut at 120 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Fit the shift shaft and drum locator
steps.instruction: Slide in the shift shaft with its washer. Hold the sliding plate away, fit the shift drum locating unit and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the locking lever with its washer, sleeve and spring and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Shift through every gear
steps.instruction: Slip the shift lever on temporarily and, while turning the main shaft, click up and down through all five gears and neutral.
verification: Every gear and neutral engages cleanly.

steps.title: Fit the pump idler, starter idler and torque limiter
steps.instruction: Fit the oil pump idler gear with its washer and secure it with the washer and lock ring. Fit the starter intermediate gear with its groove facing out, then the torque limiter, and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the clutch basket and hub
steps.instruction: Oil and fit the collar bushing and needle bearings, slide the basket on and turn the oil pump gear until the basket teeth mesh. Fit the thrust washer with its teeth lined up with the holes in the main shaft, then the inner hub. Inspect the wedge lock washers, fit them with the nut, hold the hub with the holding wrench and torque the nut to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft).
verification: Basket meshed with the pump gear.
Hub nut at 100 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Stack the clutch discs
steps.instruction: Soak the friction discs in engine oil. Start with the 1.0 mm (0.039 in) steel marked S, then alternate frictions with the seven 1.4 mm (0.055 in) steels, and finish with the other 1.0 mm steel.
verification: Thin steels at both ends of the stack.

steps.title: Fit the clutch spring stack
steps.instruction: Fit the throw-out and the pressure cap, then the pretension ring with TOP facing up and the spring washer. Fit the spring retainer with marking 1 and torque its screws in a criss-cross order to 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Check the clutch spring washer is flat
steps.instruction: Lay a straightedge across the spring washer and check the gap with feeler blades; it must be 0 to 0.10 mm (0 to 0.0039 in). If it is out, refit with the retainer marked 2 and check again, then 3. If none brings it in, replace the friction discs.
verification: Distortion recorded and in range; retainer marking noted.

steps.title: Fit the clutch cover with the balancer in time
steps.instruction: Fit a new gasket and check the dowels. With the crank still locked at TDC, set the balancer shaft with its locking screw so that its mark lines up with the tool. Ease the cover on without folding the crank seal lip, remove the balancer locking screw, and torque the M6x25 and M6x55 screws in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Balancer mark aligned before the cover went on.

steps.title: Fit the impeller and water pump cover
steps.instruction: Fit the two-part impeller and torque its nut with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Fit the cover with a new gasket, start the M6x20, M6x45 and the M6x25 drain screw with a new seal ring and Loctite 243, then tighten them evenly to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Impeller turns; cover screws at 10 Nm.

steps.title: Fit the push rod and starter
steps.instruction: Slide the clutch push rod back in. Fit the starter motor with its new O-ring and torque its screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the rotor
steps.instruction: Check the woodruff key is seated, slide the rotor on with its slot over the key, and torque the rotor screw to 70 Nm (51.6 lb-ft) with the crank locked.
verification: Rotor screw at 70 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Fit the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Check the small clutch-lubrication oil nozzle in the cover's sealing face is clear. Fit a new gasket over the dowels and torque the cover screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Hand back to the top-end guide
steps.instruction: Confirm the crank is locked at TDC, the timing chain is tied up and the case mouth is covered. Return to the top-end guide at step prep-cylinder-fit.
verification: Bottom end closed and records complete.

entry_state: Engine on the work stand with the cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed, oil drained, filter out and crank locked at TDC with the locking screw (the top-end guide the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job paused at step branch-bottom-end).
Engine sprocket, shift lever and clutch slave cylinder already off (done in the "Take the engine out of the frame" job).
exit_state: Bottom end rebuilt and closed on the work stand: cases sealed, crank end play recorded in spec, gears shift through all positions, oil pumps, timing chain, rails, primary drive, clutch, balancer, water pump, rotor, clutch and alternator covers, push rod and starter fitted. Crank locked at TDC and the timing chain tied up. Return to the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job at step prep-cylinder-fit.
title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps
completeness: Covers stripping both sides, splitting the cases, inspecting and measuring the crank, gearbox, shift parts, clutch, pumps and starter drive, changing case bearings and seals, and closing the cases; the connecting rod and crank pin pressing job is a specialist hand-off.
excluded: Pressing the crankshaft apart and rebuilding the connecting rod (specialist hand-off)
Crankcase repair or welding
Stator rewinding or electrical testing beyond the starter bench test
XC-F US six-speed gearbox (different gear stack)
Top-end work (separate guide)

required_tools.name: Water pump bearing pressing tool (KTM 79429006000) and seal pressing tool (KTM 60029043040)
Oven able to hold 150 C (302 F) for case halves, and a flat wooden board
Bearing drivers, internal bearing puller and a small press
Dial gauge with magnetic or case-mounted stand, V-blocks or roller blocks
Feeler gauge (KTM 79129941000 or equivalent) and straightedge
12-V power supply with leads for the starter test

required_parts.name: Full engine gasket set: clutch cover, alternator cover and water pump cover gaskets
required_parts.purpose: Every gasket is renewed at the major service and whenever the joint is opened.

required_parts.name: Loctite 5910 case sealant
required_parts.purpose: Seals the case joint; there is no case gasket.

required_parts.name: Crankshaft seal for the clutch cover, countershaft seal, shift shaft seal and water pump shaft seal
required_parts.purpose: Seals disturbed during the rebuild are not reused.

required_parts.name: Case bearings (main, gearbox, shift drum) and matching crank main bearing inner races
required_parts.purpose: All engine bearings are renewed at the major service.

required_parts.name: New lock rings for the gearbox shafts
required_parts.purpose: Gearbox lock rings are replaced every time.

required_parts.name: Suction oil pump
required_parts.purpose: Replaced at the major service.

required_parts.name: Timing chain and crank timing sprocket
required_parts.purpose: Chain is renewed at the major service; the sprocket is usually ruined if pulled off the crank.

required_parts.name: Freewheel
required_parts.purpose: Replaced at the major service.

required_parts.name: Connecting rod kit with bearing and crank pin
required_parts.purpose: For the specialist crank rebuild at the major service.

required_parts.name: Clutch friction discs and steels as needed
required_parts.purpose: Only if inspection or the pack thickness check calls for them.

required_parts.name: Starter motor O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Renewed at every removal.

required_parts.name: Oil pressure control valve sealing washer
required_parts.purpose: Renewed when the plug is removed.

required_parts.name: Engine oil SAE 10W/50 and assembly grease
required_parts.purpose: Assembly lube for every bearing, gear and seal lip.

required_parts.name: Loctite 243, 222 and 2701
required_parts.purpose: Thread lockers called for on internal fasteners.

prerequisites: Top end removed per the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job up to step branch-bottom-end.
Spotless bench, plenty of labelled trays, and a phone to photograph each layer before it comes apart.
Access to an oven for heating the case halves and a press or a shop that has one.
Arrangements made with a crankshaft specialist if the crank needs rebuilding.
critical_stop_conditions: Any new case bearing that is loose in its bore once the case has cooled: that case half must be replaced, not glued.
Crank run-out above 0.03 mm (0.0012 in) at either bearing pin, or rod side play outside 0.20 to 0.45 mm: crank goes to the specialist.
Crank end play outside 0.50 to 0.80 mm after shimming: do not seal the cases.
Oil pump rotor clearances over 0.20 mm (0.0079 in), or oil pressure valve spring shorter than 22.1 mm (0.87 in): replace before assembly.
Case halves will not close without pulling them together with the screws: stop, split again and find the misplaced part.
Gearbox will not shift through every gear on the bench, or the balancer marks cannot be aligned with the crank at TDC: stop before fitting the clutch cover.
Never clamp the crank by its pin in a vise and hammer on it; the webs twist and the crank is scrap.

steps.title: Confirm the starting position
steps.instruction: Check the crank is locked at TDC with the locking screw, the case mouth is covered with a clean rag and the timing chain is tied up. Photograph the clutch side and the alternator side before anything comes off.

steps.title: Remove the starter motor
steps.instruction: Remove the starter motor screws and pull the motor out of the case. Bag it with its screws.

steps.title: Pull out the clutch push rod
steps.instruction: Slide the clutch push rod out of the main shaft from the slave cylinder side and keep it straight and clean.

steps.title: Remove the water pump cover
steps.instruction: Remove the screws from the water pump cover, noting which screw goes where by length, and lift the cover off with its gasket.

steps.title: Remove the impeller
steps.instruction: Undo the nut on the impeller and pull the impeller off its shaft.

steps.title: Take off the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover screws and draw the cover off; the balancer shaft comes out with it. Lift the gasket and keep the dowels.

steps.title: Unload the clutch spring retainer
steps.instruction: Back the spring retainer screws out a little at a time in a criss-cross order so the diaphragm spring unloads evenly. Lift off the spring retainer, the spring washer, the pretension ring and the pressure cap.
verification: All four parts off and kept in order.

steps.title: Take out the clutch discs
steps.instruction: Pull the whole friction and steel stack out in one go and lay it down in its stacking order. Remove the clutch throw-out.

steps.title: Undo the inner hub nut
steps.instruction: Lock the clutch center with the KTM holding wrench and crack the hub nut loose. Remove the nut and its wedge lock washers.

steps.title: Remove the hub and basket
steps.instruction: Slide off the inner hub and the thrust washer behind it, which often sticks to the hub. Pull the clutch basket off, then remove the needle bearing and collar bushing.
verification: Hub, washer, basket, needle bearing and bushing out and kept together.

steps.title: Remove the torque limiter and starter idler
steps.instruction: Undo the screw and washer that retain the torque limiter, then lift off the limiter together with the starter idler (intermediate) gear.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump idler gear
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and washer from the oil pump idler shaft and slide the idler gear off with its washer.

steps.title: Remove the gear locking lever
steps.instruction: Undo the locking lever screw and take it out together with the lever, washer, sleeve and spring.

steps.title: Remove the shift drum locating unit
steps.instruction: Remove its screw, push the shift shaft sliding plate away from the locating unit, and lift the unit off the end of the shift drum.

steps.title: Pull out the shift shaft
steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft assembly out of the case with its washer.

steps.title: Undo the primary gear nut
steps.instruction: The primary gear nut has a left-hand thread, so turn it clockwise to loosen. With the crank still locked, break it free and remove it.

steps.title: Pull the primary gear
steps.instruction: Put the protection cap in the crank end, fit the primary gear puller and draw the gear off. Lift out the woodruff key and the freewheel gear behind it.
verification: Primary gear, key and freewheel gear off.

steps.title: Remove the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Remove the alternator cover screws and lift the cover off with its gasket. The stator stays in the cover.

steps.title: Pull the rotor
steps.instruction: With the crank still locked, remove the rotor screw. Fit the protection cap into the crank end, thread the rotor puller into the rotor, hold the puller body and turn its centre screw in until the rotor pops free. Keep the woodruff key.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain and rails
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioning rail screw and rail, then the guide rail screw, guide rails and chain clip. If the chain will be reused, mark its running direction with paint, then lift it off the crank sprocket.
verification: Chain and rails out; direction marked if reusing.

steps.title: Remove the gear position sensor
steps.instruction: Remove the two screws and take the gear position sensor off together with its protective plate.

steps.title: Remove the main shaft circlip and bushing
steps.instruction: Take the lock ring off the end of the gearbox main shaft and slide off the bushing.

steps.title: Remove the suction pump
steps.instruction: Remove the pump cover screws, the cover and its O-ring. Mark the outer face of the rotors with a felt pen, then lift out the inner and outer rotor and the drive pin.
verification: Rotors out with orientation marked; pin kept.

steps.title: Remove the force pump
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and washer from the pump drive gear, slide the gear off and take out its pin. Remove the pump cover screws and cover, draw the pump shaft out until its second pin clears the inner rotor, take that pin out, then lift out the rotors and the shaft.
verification: Force pump parts out and kept together.

steps.title: Take out the crank locking screw
steps.instruction: Remove the crankshaft locking screw; the cases cannot separate while it is engaged.

steps.title: Remove the case screws
steps.instruction: Push the case screws through a cardboard template of the case outline as you remove them, so each length goes back in its own hole.
verification: All case screws out and mapped.

steps.title: Split the cases
steps.instruction: Tilt the engine so the left case half is up, and remove the work-stand fixing arm fitting from it. Bolt the case splitting puller to the left half with suitable screws and draw the half off evenly, tapping the shaft ends if needed. Never pry between the sealing faces, and keep the half from tilting as it comes off.
verification: Left case half off without damage.

steps.title: Remove the shift rails
steps.instruction: Pull both shift rails out with their springs.

steps.title: Remove the shift drum and forks
steps.instruction: Swing the forks aside, lift the shift drum out, then take out the forks. Keep each fork's roller on its pin and tag each fork with its position.
verification: Drum and forks out; rollers kept; positions tagged.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Lift the main shaft and countershaft out together with their O-ring and washer. Check the bearing for the washer if it is not on the shaft.
verification: Both shafts out as a pair; washer found.

steps.title: Lift out the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift the crankshaft out of the right case half, then take the right half off the work stand.

steps.title: Clean the case halves
steps.instruction: Remove every trace of old sealant from both joint faces with a plastic scraper and solvent, without gouging the aluminium. Wash both halves.

steps.title: Check the oil pressure control valve
steps.instruction: Unscrew the oil pressure control valve plug from the right case and take out the spring and ball. The spring must be at least 22.1 mm (0.87 in) long. Refit the ball and spring and torque the plug with a new sealing washer to 20 Nm (14.8 lb-ft) after the case work is finished.
verification: Valve refitted at 20 Nm with new washer.

steps.title: Strip the right case half
steps.instruction: Remove the remaining dowels, the piston-cooling oil nozzle, and the bearing retainer screws and retainers over the main shaft, countershaft and shift drum bearings.
verification: Retainers and nozzle out; bearings exposed.

steps.title: Heat out the right case bearings
steps.instruction: Heat the clean right case half evenly in an oven to 150 C (302 F). Wearing heat gloves, rap the case flat onto a wooden board so the bearings drop out, and pull any that stay with a bearing puller. Take out the washer behind the bearing.
verification: All bearings due for replacement out.

steps.title: Fit new bearings in the right case
steps.instruction: Reheat the case to 150 C (302 F), refit the washer, and drop the new bearings in cold. Lay the case flat and, if needed, press them home only on the outer race until they are fully seated or flush. Let the case cool and check every bearing is tight in its bore.
verification: All bearings seated and tight when cold.

steps.title: Refit the right case retainers and nozzle
steps.instruction: Refit the bearing retainers with Loctite 243 on the screws at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Refit the piston-cooling oil nozzle with Loctite 243 at 2 Nm (1.5 lb-ft), then blow air through every oil channel.

steps.title: Strip the left case half
steps.instruction: Remove the remaining dowels, the oil spray tube and its screw, the bearing retainers, and the countershaft and shift shaft seals.

steps.title: Change the left case bearings
steps.instruction: Heat the half to 150 C (302 F) and drop the bearings out on the wooden board as before. Reheat, refit the washer, set the new cold bearings in and press home on the outer race only with the case flat. Check they are tight once cool.

steps.title: Fit the left case seals and retainers
steps.instruction: Press the new countershaft and shift shaft seals in, open side inward, until flush. Refit the bearing retainers with Loctite 243 at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and the oil spray tube screw with Loctite 243 at 2 Nm (1.5 lb-ft). Refit the dowels and blow out every oil channel.

steps.title: Renew the crank seal in the clutch cover
steps.instruction: Remove the lock ring and the old crankshaft seal from the clutch cover. Press the new seal in, open side inward, until flush, refit the lock ring and grease the sealing lip.
verification: New seal flush; lock ring seated.

steps.title: Strip the water pump
steps.instruction: Remove the balancer shaft and the water pump shaft seal from the clutch cover. Support the cover properly and press the water pump shaft bearing out toward the inside.
verification: Seal and bearing out without cracking the cover.

steps.title: Rebuild the water pump
steps.instruction: With the cover supported, press the new bearing in to its stop with the bearing pressing tool. Press the new seal fully in with the seal tool so its narrower chamfer faces the balancer shaft.
verification: Seal fully home, correct way round.

steps.title: Fit the balancer shaft into the cover
steps.instruction: Inspect the balancer shaft gear and bearing surfaces. Fit the protection cap over the water pump shaft end, slide the balancer shaft into place without cutting the seals, and remove the cap.

steps.title: Measure the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Set the crank on roller blocks with a dial gauge on each main bearing pin and turn it slowly: run-out must not exceed 0.03 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the side play between the rod big end and the crank web with a feeler gauge: 0.20 to 0.45 mm (0.0079 to 0.0177 in). Check the big end for any up-and-down play and the timing sprocket teeth for wear.

steps.title: Send the crank to a specialist if needed
steps.instruction: If any reading is out, the big end has play, or this is the major service, take the crank to a crankshaft specialist. Ask for a new rod, bearing and crank pin with the pin oil hole lined up with the web oil hole, side play set to 0.20 to 0.45 mm, run-out trued to 0.03 mm or less at both bearing pins, and the main bearing inner races and timing sprocket renewed if you are changing the case bearings or chain. Ask for the thickness of the compensating disks behind each inner race to be written down, and continue when it comes back.
verification: Crank back with a written record, or crank passed inspection.

steps.title: Check crank end play
steps.instruction: Oil the main bearings, set the crank into the right case half with the dowels in, and fit the left half dry with no sealant. Torque the case screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Mount a dial gauge on the crank end and push and pull the crank: end play must be 0.50 to 0.80 mm (0.0197 to 0.0315 in).

steps.title: Correct end play if needed
steps.instruction: If the end play is too small, the alternator-side inner race comes off and a compensating disk is removed; if too large, one is added. The clutch side normally carries a 0.2 mm disk. Pull and refit the inner race with the heated puller (heat it to 150 C (302 F) for removal and 120 C (248 F) for fitting), or have the specialist do it, then re-check and split the cases again.
verification: End play in range and recorded.

steps.title: Measure both oil pumps
steps.instruction: Fit each pump's rotors in their bores and use feeler blades between the outer rotor and the case, and between the outer and inner rotor. Both gaps must be 0.20 mm (0.0079 in) or less. Replace the suction pump regardless at the major service.

steps.title: Strip the main shaft
steps.instruction: Clamp the main shaft in soft jaws with the geared end down. Remove the parts one at a time and lay them out in order on a clean rag, photographing as you go: stop disk, second gear, fourth gear, needle bearing, stop disk, lock ring, third gear, lock ring, stop disk, fifth gear and its bushing.

steps.title: Strip the countershaft
steps.instruction: Clamp the countershaft the same way and remove the parts in order: stop disk, first gear, needle bearing, stop disk, fifth gear, lock ring, stop disk, third gear, needle bearing, stop disk, lock ring, fourth gear, lock ring, stop disk, second gear and needle bearing. Lay them out in order.

steps.title: Inspect the gearbox
steps.instruction: Check every needle bearing, the shaft journals and splines, the gear teeth and the gear bores for pitting, chips or bluing. Look at the engagement dogs and slots: rounded or chipped dogs mean that gear pair is replaced. Slide each sliding gear on its shaft splines; it must move freely. Check the stop disks for wear.
verification: Each gear pair passed or tagged for replacement.

steps.title: Inspect the shift drum, forks and rails
steps.instruction: Look at the fork pads for wear or bluing and the drum grooves for wear. Check the drum turns smoothly in its bearing. Roll the fork rails on a flat surface for bend and check their springs, and slide each fork on its rail for scoring or stiffness.
verification: Forks, drum and rails passed or tagged.

steps.title: Check the shift shaft
steps.instruction: Grip the shift shaft by its short end in soft vise jaws. Fit the sliding plate guide-pin down onto the shift quadrant, then the pressure spring, spring guide, return spring with its offset end up and over the abutment bolt, and the stop disk. Check the sliding plate contact areas and return surface for notches, then measure the gap between the sliding plate and the quadrant: 0.40 to 0.80 mm (0.0157 to 0.0315 in).

steps.title: Check the starter drive
steps.instruction: Inspect the teeth and bearings of the starter intermediate gear, torque limiter and freewheel gear. Briefly connect the starter motor to a 12-V supply, case to negative and terminal to positive; it must spin. Fit a new O-ring to the starter.

steps.title: Check or change the freewheel
steps.instruction: Fit the freewheel gear into the back of the primary gear while turning the primary gear clockwise. The primary gear must turn clockwise and lock counterclockwise. To change the freewheel, squeeze off its expansion ring, take out the old one, oil and fit the new one facing the same way, and refit the ring so all its lugs pass through the freewheel slots into the groove.
verification: Freewheel locks in one direction only.

steps.title: Inspect the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Check the throw-out, the push rod on a flat surface for bend, the spring retainer, spring washer, pretension ring and pressure cap for wear. Check the inner hub, the damping rubbers and the basket slots for notching, and the needle bearing and bushing. Steels must be flat and unpitted and frictions free of bluing or scoring; measure the pack thickness, which must be at least 26.4 mm (1.039 in).

steps.title: Rebuild the main shaft
steps.instruction: Oil every part and use new lock rings. With the geared end down in soft jaws, fit the needle bearing and fifth gear, a stop disk and lock ring, third gear with its collar down, a lock ring, a stop disk and needle bearing, fourth gear, second gear and a final stop disk. Spin every gear to check it turns freely.
verification: Stack matches the order; all gears free.

steps.title: Rebuild the countershaft
steps.instruction: With the toothed end down in soft jaws, fit the needle bearing and second gear, stop disk and lock ring, fourth gear with its fork groove down, lock ring and stop disk, needle bearing and third gear, stop disk and lock ring, fifth gear and stop disk, needle bearing and first gear, and a final stop disk. Spin every gear to check it turns freely.
verification: Stack matches the order; all gears free.

steps.title: Set the crank into the right case
steps.instruction: Mount the right case half on the work stand. Oil the main bearing and lower the crankshaft into it.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Oil the gearbox bearings and drop both gearbox shafts in as a pair, making sure the washer and O-ring are on.

steps.title: Fit the forks, drum and rails
steps.instruction: Put the fork with the smaller bore into the main shaft groove, and the other two into the lower and upper countershaft grooves. Drop the shift drum into its bearing, swing each fork's roller into its drum track, and slide both rails in with their springs.
verification: Every roller in its drum track.

steps.title: Apply case sealant
steps.instruction: Check the dowels are in, degrease both joint faces and lay a thin, even bead of Loctite 5910 on the left case half.

steps.title: Close the cases
steps.instruction: Lower the left half over the shafts, tapping lightly with a rubber mallet while turning the gearbox shafts until the faces meet; never use the screws to draw the halves together. Fit the M6x80 screws, then the M6x65 screws, and torque them all in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Refit the cap on the work-stand fixing arm.

steps.title: Fit the suction pump
steps.instruction: Oil the pump shaft and rotors. Slide the pump shaft in, fit the needle roller, fit the suction pump rotors as marked, a new O-ring and the cover, and torque the cover screws with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the main shaft bushing and circlip
steps.instruction: Slide the bushing onto the main shaft and fit a new lock ring.
verification: Lock ring fully in its groove.

steps.title: Lock the crank at TDC again
steps.instruction: Turn the crank until the notch shows in the locking screw hole and screw the crankshaft locking screw in.

steps.title: Fit the force pump
steps.instruction: Oil the rotors and fit them with the rounded side toward the case, then fit the pin. Fit the cover with its part number facing out and torque the screws with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Fit the drive pin, the pump gear, its washer and the lock ring, and turn the gear by hand to check it is free.

steps.title: Fit the gear position sensor
steps.instruction: Fit the gear position sensor with its protective plate and torque the screws with Loctite 243 to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the timing chain and rails
steps.instruction: Loop the chain onto the crank sprocket, keeping the marked direction if reused. Fit the guide rails and chain clip and torque the clip screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the tensioning rail and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Tie the chain up.

steps.title: Fit the primary gear
steps.instruction: Fit the freewheel gear and the woodruff key, then slide the primary gear on with its slot over the key. Thread on the left-hand nut (turn counterclockwise) and torque it to 120 Nm (88.5 lb-ft) with the crank locked.
verification: Primary nut at 120 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Fit the shift shaft and drum locator
steps.instruction: Slide in the shift shaft with its washer. Hold the sliding plate away, fit the shift drum locating unit and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the locking lever with its washer, sleeve and spring and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Shift through every gear
steps.instruction: Slip the shift lever on temporarily and, while turning the main shaft, click up and down through all five gears and neutral.
verification: Every gear and neutral engages cleanly.

steps.title: Fit the pump idler, starter idler and torque limiter
steps.instruction: Fit the oil pump idler gear with its washer and secure it with the washer and lock ring. Fit the starter intermediate gear with its groove facing out, then the torque limiter, and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the clutch basket and hub
steps.instruction: Oil and fit the collar bushing and needle bearings, slide the basket on and turn the oil pump gear until the basket teeth mesh. Fit the thrust washer with its teeth lined up with the holes in the main shaft, then the inner hub. Inspect the wedge lock washers, fit them with the nut, hold the hub with the holding wrench and torque the nut to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft).
verification: Basket meshed with the pump gear.
Hub nut at 100 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Stack the clutch discs
steps.instruction: Soak the friction discs in engine oil. Start with the 1.0 mm (0.039 in) steel marked S, then alternate frictions with the seven 1.4 mm (0.055 in) steels, and finish with the other 1.0 mm steel.
verification: Thin steels at both ends of the stack.

steps.title: Fit the clutch spring stack
steps.instruction: Fit the throw-out and the pressure cap, then the pretension ring with TOP facing up and the spring washer. Fit the spring retainer with marking 1 and torque its screws in a criss-cross order to 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Check the clutch spring washer is flat
steps.instruction: Lay a straightedge across the spring washer and check the gap with feeler blades; it must be 0 to 0.10 mm (0 to 0.0039 in). If it is out, refit with the retainer marked 2 and check again, then 3. If none brings it in, replace the friction discs.
verification: Distortion recorded and in range; retainer marking noted.

steps.title: Fit the clutch cover with the balancer in time
steps.instruction: Fit a new gasket and check the dowels. With the crank still locked at TDC, set the balancer shaft with its locking screw so that its mark lines up with the tool. Ease the cover on without folding the crank seal lip, remove the balancer locking screw, and torque the M6x25 and M6x55 screws in a criss-cross order to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Balancer mark aligned before the cover went on.

steps.title: Fit the impeller and water pump cover
steps.instruction: Fit the two-part impeller and torque its nut with Loctite 243 to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Fit the cover with a new gasket, start the M6x20, M6x45 and the M6x25 drain screw with a new seal ring and Loctite 243, then tighten them evenly to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Impeller turns; cover screws at 10 Nm.

steps.title: Fit the push rod and starter
steps.instruction: Slide the clutch push rod back in. Fit the starter motor with its new O-ring and torque its screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the rotor
steps.instruction: Check the woodruff key is seated, slide the rotor on with its slot over the key, and torque the rotor screw to 70 Nm (51.6 lb-ft) with the crank locked.
verification: Rotor screw at 70 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Fit the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Check the small clutch-lubrication oil nozzle in the cover's sealing face is clear. Fit a new gasket over the dowels and torque the cover screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Hand back to the top-end guide
steps.instruction: Confirm the crank is locked at TDC, the timing chain is tied up and the case mouth is covered. Return to the top-end guide at step prep-cylinder-fit.
verification: Bottom end closed and records complete.

entry_state: Complete engine on the work stand with valve clearance verified, oil filter and screens fitted and no oil or coolant (exit of the "Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston" job).
Chassis on the lift stand, strapped, with swingarm pulled back and subframe propped up, as left by the "Take the engine out of the frame" job.
exit_state: Engine mounted and every mount, linkage, control, hose, connector and body part refitted and torqued; battery reconnected. Engine still has no oil or coolant. Continue with the "Fill, first start and break-in after an engine rebuild" job.

completeness: Covers lifting the engine in and refitting mounts, swingarm, linkage, drive, controls, wiring, hoses, exhaust, airbox cover, tank and seat; filling fluids and starting are in the next guide.
excluded: Filling oil and coolant and first start (next guide)
Chain adjustment and drivetrain wear checks
Clutch hydraulic bleeding unless the lever was pulled while the slave was off

required_tools.name: Engine work stand holder and fitting
Metric sockets, hex and Torx bits

required_parts.name: Clutch slave cylinder gasket
required_parts.purpose: A new gasket goes on at every refit.

required_parts.name: Loctite 243 and 2701
required_parts.purpose: Shift lever, engine braces, sprocket screw and subframe screws.

required_parts.name: Master link for the chain
required_parts.purpose: Fit a new link if the old clip or plates are worn or bent.

required_parts.name: Cable ties
required_parts.purpose: To re-secure the harness and frame protectors.

prerequisites: Removal photos to hand for harness and hose routing.
All bagged chassis hardware from the removal guide laid out by area.
Frame mounting faces and the swingarm pivot area clean.
critical_stop_conditions: Swingarm pivot shaft will not slide through without heavy force: stop and realign the engine and swingarm rather than hammering it.
Any wire or hose pinched between the engine and the frame: free it before tightening the mounts.
Clutch lever was pulled while the slave cylinder was off: push the slave piston back and bleed the clutch before riding.
Fuel line coupling not fully latched or leaks: do not continue to the start guide.

steps.title: Take the engine off the work stand
steps.instruction: With your helper or a hoist, unbolt the engine from the work stand and remove the holder fitting from the engine.

steps.title: Lift the engine into the frame
steps.instruction: Check the frame tubes are still padded. With a helper, lower the engine into the frame from the side, watching the radiators and harness. Start the engine carrying screws but leave them loose.
verification: Engine in the frame; carrying screws started.

steps.title: Fit the swingarm pivot
steps.instruction: Bring the swingarm forward into line with the engine. Slide the pivot shaft through swingarm and engine and torque the pivot nut to 100 Nm (73.8 lb-ft).

steps.title: Torque the engine carrying screws
steps.instruction: Torque the engine carrying screws to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Carrying screws at 60 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Reconnect the linkage
steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm slightly to line up the linkage lever with the angle lever, fit the bolt and torque the nut to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).

steps.title: Seat the throttle body
steps.instruction: Remove the tape from the intake and throttle body. Push the throttle body fully onto the cylinder head intake and torque its clamp screw to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft).
verification: Throttle body fully on and square.

steps.title: Fit the shift lever
steps.instruction: Slide the shift lever onto the spline at your paint mark and torque its screw with Loctite 243 to 14 Nm (10.3 lb-ft). Make sure it does not touch the frame or case through its travel.
verification: Lever at its old position and clear of everything.

steps.title: Refit the clutch slave cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the block from the clutch lever. Fit the slave cylinder with a new gasket and torque its screws to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the engine sprocket
steps.instruction: Slide the sprocket on with its collar facing the engine. Apply Loctite 2701 and start the screw with its washer, but do not tighten it yet.
verification: Sprocket on the right way round.

steps.title: Join the chain
steps.instruction: Route the chain over both sprockets and join it with the master link. The closed end of the clip must point in the direction the chain travels.
verification: Clip fitted and pointing the right way.

steps.title: Torque the sprocket screw
steps.instruction: Have your helper hold the rear brake on and torque the sprocket screw to 60 Nm (44.3 lb-ft).
verification: Sprocket screw at 60 Nm; sign off.

steps.title: Fit the sprocket cover
steps.instruction: Fit the engine sprocket cover. Torque the M6 screw to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) and the M8 screw to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).

steps.title: Reconnect the radiator hoses
steps.instruction: Push both radiator hoses fully onto their engine stubs, set the clamps in their original positions and tighten them.
verification: Both hoses fully on and clamped.

steps.title: Reconnect the head sensor and plug cap
steps.instruction: Plug in the sensor connector on the cylinder head and slide its rubber cap back over it. Push the spark plug connector firmly onto the plug.

steps.title: Reconnect the starter cable
steps.instruction: Fit the positive cable to the starter motor, tighten its nut to 4 Nm (3 lb-ft) and slide the protective cap over it.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine harness
steps.instruction: Plug in the crankshaft speed sensor, alternator and gear position sensor connectors. Route the wiring exactly as in your photos, away from heat and moving parts, and secure it with its clamp and new cable ties.

steps.title: Fit the engine braces
steps.instruction: Fit both engine braces. Torque the screws into the engine with Loctite 243 and the screws into the frame with Loctite 2701, all to 25 Nm (18.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Lower the subframe
steps.instruction: Lower the subframe, guiding the intake boot over the throttle body. Fit the screws with Loctite 2701 and torque the lower screws to 30 Nm (22.1 lb-ft) and the upper screws to 35 Nm (25.8 lb-ft) on both sides. Tighten the intake boot clamp.
verification: Boot fully on the throttle body.

steps.title: Refit the frame protectors
steps.instruction: Fit the left protector, then slide the right one in from below and push it back. Torque the screws to 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft) and secure the protectors with cable ties.

steps.title: Fit the header pipe
steps.instruction: Remove the rag from the exhaust port. Fit the header into the port, hook on its springs with the spring hook, and torque the screw on the cylinder head brace to 15 Nm (11.1 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the silencer
steps.instruction: Slide the silencer onto the header, start its screws with washers, hook on the spring, then torque the screws to the general chassis value for their thread size: M6 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), M8 25 Nm (18.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the air filter box cover
steps.instruction: Uncover the air filter, check it is seated, then clip the cover in. If your cover uses a screw, torque it to 3 Nm (2.2 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the fuel tank
steps.instruction: Check the throttle cables are routed correctly, set the tank on, and slide the spoilers onto the radiators without trapping any cable. Reattach the breather hose, torque the spoiler screws to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and the front screw with its rubber bushing to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Plug in the fuel pump connector. Take off the wash caps, blow both halves clean, wipe a little silicone spray onto the coupling O-ring with a lint-free cloth and snap the coupling together. Keep the line and cable well away from the exhaust.

steps.title: Fit the seat
steps.instruction: Hook the front of the seat onto its collar bushings, push it back until the rear lugs engage, and torque the seat screw to 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Reconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Reconnect the negative battery cable and torque the terminal screw to 2.5 Nm (1.84 lb-ft).

steps.title: Do a full walk-around
steps.instruction: With your photos and record sheet, go over every fastener, clamp, connector and cable you touched. Pull the clutch lever and check it feels firm, twist the throttle and check it snaps closed, and check the rear wheel turns with the chain.

title: Fill, first start and break-in after an engine rebuild
completeness: Covers filling oil and coolant, checking the clutch fluid, first start, leak and temperature checks, idle, dealer initialization, quickshifter teach, the break-in rides and the one-hour checks; it does not give a timed break-in schedule because none is published for this model.
excluded: Fork, shock and brake service
Suspension setup
Fuel pressure test (dealer tool)
Throttle position sensor adjustment

required_tools.name: Crankshaft locking screw (KTM 61229015000) and spark plug wrench (KTM 77229172000)
Tachometer able to read idle speed
Bleed syringe (KTM 50329050000) with hose, if the clutch needs bleeding
Fire extinguisher and good ventilation or exhaust extraction

required_parts.name: Engine oil SAE 10W/50, JASO T903 MA2, fully synthetic, 1.20 l (1.27 qt)
required_parts.purpose: Total engine oil capacity.

required_parts.name: Coolant: silicate-free with aluminium corrosion inhibitor, frost protection to at least -25 C (-13 F); premix recommended, 0.95 l (1 qt)
required_parts.purpose: Cooling system fill; never plain water.

required_parts.name: Brake fluid DOT 4 or DOT 5.1
required_parts.purpose: For topping up or bleeding the clutch.

required_parts.name: Fresh oil filter and drain plug seal ring
required_parts.purpose: For the oil change after break-in.

required_parts.name: Fuel: unleaded ROZ 95, up to E10
required_parts.purpose: Fill the tank before starting.

prerequisites: Engine refit guide completed and walk-around signed off.
Bike upright on level ground for filling and level checks.
Outdoors or with exhaust extraction; never run the engine in a closed room.
A dealer appointment for the diagnostics-tool initialization run.
critical_stop_conditions: No oil level showing after filling, or oil visible in the coolant or coolant in the oil: do not start.
Knocking, metallic rattling or a loud valvetrain clatter that does not settle within seconds of starting: shut off immediately.
Any oil, coolant or fuel leak while running: shut off and fix it before continuing.
Coolant boiling out of the overflow, or one radiator staying cold while the other is hot: shut off; air lock or water pump fault.
Engine fails to start after six attempts: stop cranking and find the fault.
Any valve clearance out of range at the one-hour check: correct it before the bike is ridden again.

steps.title: Fill the engine oil
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright. Remove the oil filler plug with its O-ring and pour in 1.20 l (1.27 qt) of SAE 10W/50 engine oil. Refit the filler plug with its O-ring.
verification: Oil level visible in the sight glass.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Confirm the drain screw on the water pump cover is tight. With the bike upright, slowly pour coolant into the radiator until it sits 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins, squeezing the hoses to push air out; the system holds about 0.95 l (1 qt). Refit the radiator cap.
verification: Coolant 10 mm above the fins; cap on.

steps.title: Check the clutch fluid
steps.instruction: Turn the clutch reservoir on the bar level, open the cover and check the fluid is 4 mm (0.16 in) below the top edge, topping up with DOT 4 or 5.1 if needed. Pull the lever several times; it must feel firm.

steps.title: Bleed the clutch if the lever is soft
steps.instruction: If the lever feels spongy, fill the bleed syringe with fresh fluid, connect it with a hose to the slave cylinder bleeder and open the bleeder slightly. Push fluid up until it comes out of the reservoir hole with no bubbles, draining the reservoir now and then so it does not overflow. Close the bleeder, reset the level to 4 mm below the edge and refit the cover.

steps.title: Do the pre-start check
steps.instruction: Put fuel in the tank. Check under the bike for drips, confirm the throttle snaps shut, the transmission is in neutral and no tools or rags are left on the engine. Make sure there is ventilation and an extinguisher within reach.
verification: No leaks, neutral selected, area safe.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.instruction: When the air is colder than 20 C (68 F), press the cold start knob fully in first. Press the start button for no more than 5 seconds at a time with the throttle closed, waiting 15 seconds between tries. After six failed tries, stop and find the fault.

steps.title: Warm it up gently
steps.instruction: Let the engine warm at idle and light throttle only, never revving it hard while cold. Listen for unusual noise and watch the exhaust for blue or white smoke that does not clear.
verification: Engine runs smoothly without strange noise.

steps.title: Check for leaks and even heating
steps.instruction: While it warms, look at every joint you opened: head, base, covers, plugs, hoses and the oil filter cover. Carefully feel the radiator hoses and both radiators as they warm; they should heat up together. Shut off at once if anything leaks or the coolant boils.

steps.title: Check the idle speed
steps.instruction: With the engine fully warm and the cold start button back in its normal position, read the idle speed: 2,200 to 2,300 rpm. Adjust with the idle screw on the throttle body if needed; clockwise raises it.

steps.title: Check the oil level warm
steps.instruction: Shut off, wait one minute with the bike upright, and read the sight glass. Oil should sit between the middle and the top of the glass. Top up with the same oil if it is low.

steps.title: Re-check coolant once cold
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool completely. Open the radiator cap and top up to 10 mm (0.39 in) above the fins, since trapped air will have worked out. Check the antifreeze protection with a tester; it should read between -25 and -45 C (-13 and -49 F).
verification: Coolant topped up; antifreeze reading recorded.

steps.title: Have the dealer reset the engine management
steps.instruction: Take the bike to a KTM dealer with the diagnostics tool. Ask them to clear the adaptation values, program the gear position sensor, run the initialization run and read out the fault memory. Ride only after it reports a successful initialization.
verification: Initialization successful and fault memory clear.

steps.title: Teach the quickshifter
steps.instruction: Start the engine. Hold the QS button for at least 10 seconds until the QS lamp flashes, pull in the clutch, click into first and keep the shift lever pressed all the way down, then tap the QS button. The lamp turns blue when it has learned; if not, repeat.

steps.title: First break-in ride
steps.instruction: Ride a short, easy session: smooth throttle, keep varying the revs, short-shift and avoid full throttle and long periods at the same speed. Do not lug it in a high gear either. Follow the piston or ring maker's break-in times if they give them.

steps.title: Cool down and check after each session
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool fully after the session. Check the oil level, the coolant level and look for leaks before the next ride.

steps.title: Build up the load gradually
steps.instruction: Over the following sessions, use more throttle and revs step by step until you are riding normally. Stop and investigate any new noise, smoke, leak or loss of power.
verification: Engine pulls cleanly with no new symptoms.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance after one hour
steps.instruction: After the first operating hour, with the engine at room temperature, remove the seat, tank, spark plug and valve cover, lock the crank at TDC and measure all four valves: intake 0.10 to 0.15 mm, exhaust 0.12 to 0.17 mm. Correct with shims if any is out, then refit the parts at the same torques as in the top-end guide.
verification: All four clearances recorded and in range.

steps.title: Do the one-hour checks
steps.instruction: Check chain tension and the sprocket screw, then go over every screw, nut and hose clamp on the bike for tightness. Replace the fuel screen, check the coolant level, and have the fault memory read out after a test ride.

steps.title: Change the oil after break-in
steps.instruction: Drain the oil warm, clean both oil screens, look closely at the drain magnet for metal, and fit a new filter and drain plug seal ring at the same torques as before. Refill with 1.20 l (1.27 qt) and check the level.

steps.title: Log the rebuild hours
steps.instruction: Write down the hour meter reading and the work done so the next minor (45 hour) and major (90 hour) engine services can be planned from this point.
verification: Hour meter and rebuild summary recorded.
