exit_state: Engine filled, started, leak-free, run in, re-checked after the first operating hour (valve clearance, fasteners, chain, fluids) and adaptation values reset by a dealer: bike ready to ride.
title: Fill, first start and break-in after an engine rebuild
completeness: Covers filling oil and coolant, checking the clutch fluid, first start, leak and temperature checks, idle, dealer initialization, quickshifter teach, the break-in rides and the one-hour checks; it does not give a timed break-in schedule because none is published for this model.
excluded: Fork, shock and brake service
Suspension setup
Fuel pressure test (dealer tool)
Throttle position sensor adjustment

required_tools.name: Crankshaft locking screw (KTM 61229015000) and spark plug wrench (KTM 77229172000)
Tachometer able to read idle speed
Bleed syringe (KTM 50329050000) with hose, if the clutch needs bleeding
Fire extinguisher and good ventilation or exhaust extraction

required_parts.name: Engine oil SAE 10W/50, JASO T903 MA2, fully synthetic, 1.20 l (1.27 qt)
required_parts.purpose: Total engine oil capacity.

required_parts.name: Coolant: silicate-free with aluminium corrosion inhibitor, frost protection to at least -25 C (-13 F); premix recommended, 0.95 l (1 qt)
required_parts.purpose: Cooling system fill; never plain water.

required_parts.name: Brake fluid DOT 4 or DOT 5.1
required_parts.purpose: For topping up or bleeding the clutch.

required_parts.name: Fresh oil filter and drain plug seal ring
required_parts.purpose: For the oil change after break-in.

required_parts.name: Fuel: unleaded ROZ 95, up to E10
required_parts.purpose: Fill the tank before starting.

prerequisites: Engine refit guide completed and walk-around signed off.
Bike upright on level ground for filling and level checks.
Outdoors or with exhaust extraction; never run the engine in a closed room.
A dealer appointment for the diagnostics-tool initialization run.
critical_stop_conditions: No oil level showing after filling, or oil visible in the coolant or coolant in the oil: do not start.
Knocking, metallic rattling or a loud valvetrain clatter that does not settle within seconds of starting: shut off immediately.
Any oil, coolant or fuel leak while running: shut off and fix it before continuing.
Coolant boiling out of the overflow, or one radiator staying cold while the other is hot: shut off; air lock or water pump fault.
Engine fails to start after six attempts: stop cranking and find the fault.
Any valve clearance out of range at the one-hour check: correct it before the bike is ridden again.

steps.title: Fill the engine oil
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright. Remove the oil filler plug with its O-ring and pour in 1.20 l (1.27 qt) of SAE 10W/50 engine oil. Refit the filler plug with its O-ring.
verification: Oil level visible in the sight glass.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Confirm the drain screw on the water pump cover is tight. With the bike upright, slowly pour coolant into the radiator until it sits 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins, squeezing the hoses to push air out; the system holds about 0.95 l (1 qt). Refit the radiator cap.
verification: Coolant 10 mm above the fins; cap on.

steps.title: Check the clutch fluid
steps.instruction: Turn the clutch reservoir on the bar level, open the cover and check the fluid is 4 mm (0.16 in) below the top edge, topping up with DOT 4 or 5.1 if needed. Pull the lever several times; it must feel firm.

steps.title: Bleed the clutch if the lever is soft
steps.instruction: If the lever feels spongy, fill the bleed syringe with fresh fluid, connect it with a hose to the slave cylinder bleeder and open the bleeder slightly. Push fluid up until it comes out of the reservoir hole with no bubbles, draining the reservoir now and then so it does not overflow. Close the bleeder, reset the level to 4 mm below the edge and refit the cover.

steps.title: Do the pre-start check
steps.instruction: Put fuel in the tank. Check under the bike for drips, confirm the throttle snaps shut, the transmission is in neutral and no tools or rags are left on the engine. Make sure there is ventilation and an extinguisher within reach.
verification: No leaks, neutral selected, area safe.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.instruction: When the air is colder than 20 C (68 F), press the cold start knob fully in first. Press the start button for no more than 5 seconds at a time with the throttle closed, waiting 15 seconds between tries. After six failed tries, stop and find the fault.

steps.title: Warm it up gently
steps.instruction: Let the engine warm at idle and light throttle only, never revving it hard while cold. Listen for unusual noise and watch the exhaust for blue or white smoke that does not clear.
verification: Engine runs smoothly without strange noise.

steps.title: Check for leaks and even heating
steps.instruction: While it warms, look at every joint you opened: head, base, covers, plugs, hoses and the oil filter cover. Carefully feel the radiator hoses and both radiators as they warm; they should heat up together. Shut off at once if anything leaks or the coolant boils.

steps.title: Check the idle speed
steps.instruction: With the engine fully warm and the cold start button back in its normal position, read the idle speed: 2,200 to 2,300 rpm. Adjust with the idle screw on the throttle body if needed; clockwise raises it.

steps.title: Check the oil level warm
steps.instruction: Shut off, wait one minute with the bike upright, and read the sight glass. Oil should sit between the middle and the top of the glass. Top up with the same oil if it is low.

steps.title: Re-check coolant once cold
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool completely. Open the radiator cap and top up to 10 mm (0.39 in) above the fins, since trapped air will have worked out. Check the antifreeze protection with a tester; it should read between -25 and -45 C (-13 and -49 F).
verification: Coolant topped up; antifreeze reading recorded.

steps.title: Have the dealer reset the engine management
steps.instruction: Take the bike to a KTM dealer with the diagnostics tool. Ask them to clear the adaptation values, program the gear position sensor, run the initialization run and read out the fault memory. Ride only after it reports a successful initialization.
verification: Initialization successful and fault memory clear.

steps.title: Teach the quickshifter
steps.instruction: Start the engine. Hold the QS button for at least 10 seconds until the QS lamp flashes, pull in the clutch, click into first and keep the shift lever pressed all the way down, then tap the QS button. The lamp turns blue when it has learned; if not, repeat.

steps.title: First break-in ride
steps.instruction: Ride a short, easy session: smooth throttle, keep varying the revs, short-shift and avoid full throttle and long periods at the same speed. Do not lug it in a high gear either. Follow the piston or ring maker's break-in times if they give them.

steps.title: Cool down and check after each session
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool fully after the session. Check the oil level, the coolant level and look for leaks before the next ride.

steps.title: Build up the load gradually
steps.instruction: Over the following sessions, use more throttle and revs step by step until you are riding normally. Stop and investigate any new noise, smoke, leak or loss of power.
verification: Engine pulls cleanly with no new symptoms.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance after one hour
steps.instruction: After the first operating hour, with the engine at room temperature, remove the seat, tank, spark plug and valve cover, lock the crank at TDC and measure all four valves: intake 0.10 to 0.15 mm, exhaust 0.12 to 0.17 mm. Correct with shims if any is out, then refit the parts at the same torques as in the top-end guide.
verification: All four clearances recorded and in range.

steps.title: Do the one-hour checks
steps.instruction: Check chain tension and the sprocket screw, then go over every screw, nut and hose clamp on the bike for tightness. Replace the fuel screen, check the coolant level, and have the fault memory read out after a test ride.

steps.title: Change the oil after break-in
steps.instruction: Drain the oil warm, clean both oil screens, look closely at the drain magnet for metal, and fit a new filter and drain plug seal ring at the same torques as before. Refill with 1.20 l (1.27 qt) and check the level.

steps.title: Log the rebuild hours
steps.instruction: Write down the hour meter reading and the work done so the next minor (45 hour) and major (90 hour) engine services can be planned from this point.
verification: Hour meter and rebuild summary recorded.
